title: The culture of dress – the meaning of hijab
intro: Modesty, the Islamic way of dressing, and why Muslim women wear the hijab.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says: O Prophet, tell your wives, your daughters and the believing women to draw their outer garments over themselves. That way they will be recognised more easily and not be harassed. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Ahzab 33:59)</small>

The most important foundations of a happy and successful life are faith in Allah, growing up in a good, healthy and harmonious family, and an Islamic upbringing. The children of Muslims should be well brought up, taught the rules of Islam, and used to a basic code of good behaviour at home and in society.

Special attention should be given to bringing up girls, who, besides other good qualities, should have a strong sense of modesty (haya’). It is said: “Modesty is beautiful – and even more beautiful in a woman.”

Through the Qur’an, Allah (SWT) prescribed how a Muslim woman should behave. Among her other duties, the hijab is prescribed for her. Hijab is the way a Muslim woman dresses that covers the whole body except the face and hands.

Besides being a way of dressing, the hijab also has a deeper meaning: chastity, modesty, privacy and good morals. Allah (SWT) commanded the hijab for Muslim women, so wearing it is a Muslim woman’s answer to the command of Allah, the Most High.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: ‘A’ishah (RA) reported that Asma’, the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA), once came to the Messenger of Allah (SAW) in see-through clothes. He turned away and said: “O Asma’, when a woman becomes an adult, it is not allowed for any part of her body to be seen except this and this” – and he pointed to his face and hands. (Abu Dawud)
The hijab is a part of the religious rules about proper dress for a Muslim woman, and an outward sign of her identity. That is why it must not be tight, short or see-through.

items: Islam prescribed the hijab as part of decency and modesty between men and women. A Muslim woman who wears it is adorned with the beautiful quality of modesty. ‘Umar (RA) said: “Whoever is modest will cover; whoever covers will be mindful of Allah; and whoever is mindful of Allah will be protected.”

The hijab protects a woman from harassment. It guides her towards chastity and faithfulness to her husband, and protects her in everyday life. As Allah revealed: That way they will be recognised more easily and not be harassed. (Qur’an, Al-Ahzab 33:59)

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA) said: “The Messenger of Allah (SAW) cursed men who imitate women and women who imitate men.” (Bukhari)

Clothes are a gift from Allah (SWT). That is why the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (SAW), made this du‘a: “Praise be to Allah, who gave me nice clothes so that I look nice among people and cover what should be covered!” (Ahmad)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: A woman – in her family and in public life – was and always will be our mother, sister, wife and daughter. That is why she should be especially respected and valued.

learn.title: 🧕 World Hijab Day
learn.html: 1 February is marked as World Hijab Day. On that day we remind Muslim women that the hijab is their duty – and their safety and happiness. Allah (SWT) gave us clothes so that we can be freer and more beautiful.

practice.prompt: Tap every true sentence, then tap Check.

options.text: It covers the whole body except the face and hands
It is a Muslim woman’s answer to Allah’s command
It is an outward sign of a Muslim woman’s identity
It stands for chastity, modesty and privacy
It may be tight or see-through
options.why: The hijab must not be tight, short or see-through.
The hijab is a religious duty and a sign of modesty, not just fashion.

options: Men who imitate women and women who imitate men

practice.title: Talk with your muallim
prompts: 💬 What is hijab? What does the hijab mean for a Muslim woman? What does it protect her from?
🧕 1 February is World Hijab Day. It reminds a Muslim woman that the hijab is her duty – and her safety and happiness. Allah (SWT) gave us clothes so that we can be freer and more beautiful.
🌸 Modesty is a beautiful quality for every Muslim man and woman; its opposite is indecency in dress, speech and actions. Write how a Muslim woman, for whom the hijab is a duty, is free.

🤔 It can seem that a Muslim woman is not free because the hijab is a duty. But the hijab lets her keep her modesty and her beauty for her own home. Write why the hijab does not let her be exposed to eyes whose looks could harm her.
